# A common right descent decreases the length-thirteen Kazhdan–Lusztig coefficient by at most four

<!-- Generated by MathResearchLab. This file is rewritten on every sync; edit the app, not this file. -->

**Status:** Open per source; openness not yet verified

## Statement

Original wording (verbatim from the source):

```latex
For every uncompressible pair $x\leq w$ in $S_{12}$ with length difference thirteen, connected transposition graph, three cycles in $x^{-1}w$, and $\mu(x,w)>0$, every common right descent $s$ satisfies $\mu(x,w)-\mu(xs,ws)\leq4$.
```

Normalized:

For every $x,w\in S_{12}$ with $x\leq w$ in Bruhat order, suppose that $(x,w)$ is uncompressible, its transposition graph is connected, $\ell(w)-\ell(x)=13$, $x^{-1}w$ has exactly three cycles including fixed points, and $[q^6]P_{x,w}(q)>0$. Then for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,11\}$ such that $s=(i,i+1)$ satisfies $xs<x$ and $ws<w$, one has $[q^6]P_{x,w}(q)-[q^6]P_{xs,ws}(q)\leq4$.

Source: Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, Emily Xia Meng, Henry Kvinge, *PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models*, arXiv:2611.33966, p. 37, B.4.4 A sufficient inequality along common descents

## Definitions

- **Length and $\mu$**: $\ell(x)$ is the inversion number of $x$. For odd positive $d=\ell(w)-\ell(x)$, $\mu(x,w)=[q^{(d-1)/2}]P_{x,w}(q)$, where $P_{x,w}$ is the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomial. A common right descent lowers both endpoint lengths by one, preserving $d$.
- **Uncompressible pair**: There is no position $i$ with $x(i)=w(i)=j$ and $\#\{k<i:w(k)\geq j\}=\#\{k<i:x(k)\geq j\}$. Such a position could be deleted from both permutations, followed by relabeling.
- **Transposition graph**: Take any saturated Bruhat chain from $x$ to $w$. Its graph has the permutation positions as vertices and the position transpositions labeling the chain steps as edges. Its connected components are independent of the chain.

## Known results

- Equation (B.17) expresses the difference exactly as $[q^5]P_{x,ws}$ minus a sum of products of $\mu$-coefficients. Proposition B.4.6 shows that a hypothetical failure of length-thirteen invariance would force a difference of at least five in the specified class. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.4.4, pp. 36–37))*
- A coefficient search found a connected length-ten interval in $S_{10}$ with $G=0$ and $[q^4]P_{x,v}=8$. This rules out bounding the uncorrected top-degree term by four from connectedness and $G=0$ alone. *(Michael Ruofan Zeng, Junaid Hasan, Xuanyu Yang, PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models, arXiv:2611.33966 (B.4.4, Table 20, p. 37); computational; reproduced: None)*
